details.description: Sensitive API keys and secrets are hardcoded in source control.
details.fix_explanation: Moved secrets into environment variables and fail-safe configuration. The application now reads PAYMENT_TOKEN, MAIL_SERVER_KEY, INTERNAL_AUTH, and AUTH_TOKEN from the environment. It warns if AUTH_TOKEN is missing. This avoids leaking credentials in source control.
details.secure_code_snippet:
PAYMENT_TOKEN = os.environ.get("PAYMENT_TOKEN")
MAIL_SERVER_KEY = os.environ.get("MAIL_SERVER_KEY")
INTERNAL_AUTH = os.environ.get("INTERNAL_AUTH")
AUTH_TOKEN = os.environ.get("AUTH_TOKEN")

details.description: User tokens were generated using MD5 of username+secret which is fast and predictable.
details.fix_explanation: Replaced MD5 with HMAC-SHA256 using a server-side secret (INTERNAL_AUTH). HMAC provides keyed hashing and stronger collision resistance.
details.secure_code_snippet:
def auth_user(info):
    username = info.get("username", "")
    digest = hmac.new(INTERNAL_AUTH.encode(), username.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return digest

details.description: The SQL query was built by string interpolation with user-controlled input (uid).
details.fix_explanation: Parameterize queries using sqlite3 parameter binding and validate that uid is an integer. This prevents injection payloads from modifying the query logic.
details.secure_code_snippet: c.execute("SELECT id,name,balance FROM profiles WHERE id = ?", (uid_int,))

details.description: notify_url was accepted without validation and requests.post was called without timeout or host checks, enabling SSRF and slow HTTP attacks.
details.fix_explanation: Validate notify_url against a configured ALLOWED_NOTIFY_HOSTS list and use requests.post with a timeout and TLS verification. Reject requests to disallowed hosts.
details.secure_code_snippet:
parsed = urlparse(url)
if parsed.hostname not in ALLOWED_NOTIFY_HOSTS:
    raise ValueError("notify_url host is not allowed")
resp = requests.post(url, json={"token": PAYMENT_TOKEN, "amount": amount_val}, timeout=5, verify=True)

details.description: update_records opened arbitrary filesystem paths provided by the user, enabling reading of sensitive files.
details.fix_explanation: Restrict file reads to a configured CONFIG_DIR and verify that the requested path is under that directory to prevent traversal and arbitrary file reads.
details.secure_code_snippet:
base_dir = os.path.abspath(CONFIG_DIR)
requested = os.path.abspath(path)
if not requested.startswith(base_dir):
    raise ValueError("Access to the specified file is not allowed")
with open(requested) as f:
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)

details.description: export_data constructed shell commands and used shell=True causing command injection when name is attacker-controlled.
details.fix_explanation: Replace shell invocation with Python's zipfile module and sanitize the name. Avoids shell metacharacters and path traversal.
details.secure_code_snippet:
safe_name = os.path.basename(name)
zip_path = f"{safe_name}.zip"
with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
    zf.write(DB_FILE)

details.description: Endpoints performing sensitive actions (profile access, transfer, config, export) did not enforce authentication.
details.fix_explanation: Added a require_auth decorator and require Authorization header for these endpoints. Authentication token is configurable via AUTH_TOKEN environment variable.

details.description: app.run(debug=True) enables the Flask debugger which may allow remote code execution.
details.fix_explanation: Disabled debug mode by setting debug=False and recommended use of production WSGI servers.

details.description: Logging or printing sensitive transfer details may leak information to logs.
details.fix_explanation: Use structured logging at an appropriate level and avoid printing sensitive tokens or full payloads. The updated code logs non-sensitive information only.
details.secure_code_snippet: logger.info("Notifying payment endpoint for target %s", target)
